original_source_text: Accurate computation of the Perturbation Projection Vector (PPV) is essential for analyzing oscillator phase noise. The PPV corresponds to the steady-state solution of the adjoint system in small-signal oscillator analysis, but in large time-constant oscillators, it is often obscured by numerous slow-decaying modes. To address this, we propose a Floquet-based subspace projection (FSP) method, which confines PPV computation to a low-dimensional subspace spanned by the PPV and slow-decaying solutions. Utilizing the biorthogonality condition, we construct a linear system within this subspace to lock the PPV, since slow-decaying solutions are orthogonal to the large-signal derivative. This linear system is small-scale and can be solved directly, which results in high-accuracy PPVs. Numerical results demonstrate that FSP significantly enhances both accuracy and computational efficiency.
